summary.title: Cedar Grove volunteer portal
summary.description: Assumptions: The shared folder is on some third-party cloud service. Also, volunteers can see any file in it (there are no special permissions). Some hosting provider runs the servers and database for Cedar Grove. CSVs stay indefinitely in the shared folder and on phones. There's no retention/deletion policy.

diagrams.title: Cedar Grove volunteer portal

threats.title: A05: False Delivery Requests
threats.description: Delivery requests are processed through the web form where client information can be input. These delivery requests entered on the form could contain SQL or web-form injection that could modify or delete client data (in S1). These forms are prone to unauthorized modification which can alter client information which can affect confirmation status and client information storage.
threats.mitigation: In the webform (P1), use parameterized queries and preprocess inputs to trim and flag potentially harmful inputs (look for keywords like DELETE, DROP, ALTER, etc) so that web form inputs are now treated as text that can't modify or delete data in S1.

threats.title: A04: Mail Service Vulnerability
threats.description: Cedar Grove uses the external email service (P3) to send confirmation emails to the delivery recipients. This external service has no known backup server to rely on. If the service experiences denial of service (through an attack or simply an outage), it can delay or even make confirmation emails unavailable, where delivery recipients may not receive confirmations.
threats.mitigation: Ensure that a backup email provider is configured (in P1) which allows confirmation emails to be sent if the main service is unavailable and make sure that requests that couldn't be delivered are queued to be retried when the service(s) are back online. Implementing this makes it so that no emails are permanently lost in the event of an outage, which is also less likely due to the backup provider.

threats.title: A03: Shared Account Login Clarity
threats.description: Volunteers currently share one dispatch login account to download the weekly delivery CSVs. There are exported lists contained in the shared folder which any volunteer can access through the phone. Currently, there is no audit log when accessing the information nor tracking of individual login location/identity so in the case of a breach, actions cannot be traced back to a specific volunteer.
threats.mitigation: Deny login access from unapproved and suspicious devices and/or locations and implement individual logins instead of the dispatch login, with logging on downloads. Now, suspicious logins are blocked and each volunteer has their own login, so downloads can be traced back to them.

threats.title: A01: Exported CSV on compromised personal devices
threats.description: Volunteers download the weekly delivery CSV to their personal phones, where it stays indefinitely. If a phone is lost or compromised, an attacker could gain full access to the exported CSV containing confidential information.
threats.mitigation: Recommend that volunteer phones require biometric access such as fingerprinting or facial recognition or at least ensure a password is set. One could also limit the CSV to only the fields which contain information required for deliveries. Combining both, a breach is both less likely and less severe since there is an additional layer of security and less information.

threats.title: A02: Compromised exported CSVs
threats.description: A CSV being downloaded by the volunteer for weekly delivery records might have been tampered with by an attacker if they have edit access in the folder. The CSV can have its addresses routed to unintended locations where theft can occur. The weekly delivery list does not have an integrity check to ensure that the file details have not been affected.
threats.mitigation: Ensure that only the coordinator has edit and upload access (in S2) and everyone else can only view (and download). Now, only the coordinator could edit the file which lessens the surface area for attacks.
